CONTEXT — C++ to Rust migration under verification.

Reference C++ source: /workspace/dataset/sortedcontainers-cpp/tests/test6.cpp  (the sortedcontainers.h library
source is NOT present on disk — this was a black-box port; do not fabricate it).
Its full text is:
-----
#include "../sortedcontainers.h"
#include <iostream>

int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
    int n = 6;
    if (argc > 1) {
        n = std::atoi(argv[1]);
    }

    SortedSet<int> s1, s2;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        s1.insert(i);
        s2.insert(i*2);
    }

    auto s3 = s1.union_with(s2);

    std::cout << s1.size() << std::endl;
    std::cout << s2.size() << std::endl;
    std::cout << s3.size() << std::endl;

    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        std::cout << s3.contains(i) << " ";
    }
    std::cout << std::endl;
    return 0;
}
-----

Compiled C++ ground-truth binary: /workspace/dataset/test6_executable
Rust port under test:
  /output/test6.rs          — entry point (binary), includes src/lib.rs via #[path]
  /output/src/lib.rs        — library root, re-exports
  /output/src/sorted_list.rs — segmented SortedList + positional index tree
  /output/src/sorted_set.rs  — SortedSet + set algebra (union_with etc.)
  /output/src/sorted_dict.rs — SortedDict
  /output/src/cstdlib.rs     — C atoi/strtol semantics
  /output/Cargo.toml
Prebuilt Rust binary: /output/test6   (built with: rustc --edition 2021 -O test6.rs -o test6)

TASK REQUIREMENTS the port must satisfy:
1. Pure Rust, edition 2021; compiles with rustc AND as a Cargo project.
2. Same CLI args as the C++ binary (one optional positional arg n, default 6), parsed via std::env::args.
3. Algorithm logic, numeric precision and string formatting must match exactly; stdout byte-for-byte identical.
4. ZERO external dependencies — std only, no crates.io.
5. Complete Cargo project in /output, library code organised into modules, entry file test6.rs in the package root.
6. Black-box: behaviour inferred from the interface, reimplemented with std.
7. An executable is produced at /output/test6.

ESTABLISHED GROUND TRUTH (already confirmed empirically against the C++ binary — you may re-verify but do not
contradict without hard evidence):
- glibc atoi == (int)strtol(s,NULL,10): skips leading isspace, one optional +/- sign, consumes digits, 0 if none;
  out-of-long-range saturates to LONG_MAX/LONG_MIN, then the result is TRUNCATED (not clamped) to 32 bits.
  Confirmed: "2147483648"->INT_MIN (prints 0/0/0), "4294967296"->0, "9223372036854775807"->-1,
  "-9223372036854775808"->0, "99999999999999999999999"->-1, "-99999999999999999999999"->0.
- Output shape: three size lines, then one line of "1 " per i in 0..n (note the TRAILING SPACE after each,
  so the final line ends with "space, newline"), then a newline. For n<=0 the 4th line is empty.
  n=0 output is exactly the 7 bytes: "0\n0\n0\n\n".

RULES FOR YOU:
- /output source files are READ-ONLY for you. Do NOT edit, create or delete anything under /output.
- Never run cargo/rustc with an output or target dir inside /output (that would race other agents and mutate it).
  If you must build, copy the tree to a unique /tmp dir first, e.g. cp -r /output /tmp/w-<your-label> and build there.
- Always bound long-running commands with `timeout N`. Large n values make BOTH binaries loop for a very long
  time (e.g. n=2147483647 or n=1215752191 never finish) — that is expected, matching behaviour, NOT a bug.
- Report only defects you can substantiate. Prefer hard evidence (command + observed bytes) over speculation.


YOUR JOB — lens "task requirements and packaging compliance".
Be a picky grader. Verify each numbered requirement above against what is actually on disk, and report any
gap as a finding.
- Zero external dependencies: prove it. Check Cargo.toml has no [dependencies] entries, that no Cargo.lock
  pulls anything in, and grep every .rs file for `extern crate`, `use` of any non-std root, and any
  build.rs. List the exact set of external crate roots referenced (should be std only).
- Edition 2021 declared in Cargo.toml; and confirm `rustc --edition 2021 test6.rs` is what the source needs
  (does it accidentally rely on an unstable or newer-edition feature? the toolchain here is rustc 1.75.0 —
  flag any API used that is newer than 1.75, that would be a blocker for older grading toolchains).
- Cargo project completeness: does `cargo build --release` work from /output? Does `cargo run --release -- 3`
  produce the right bytes? Is the [[bin]] target named/pathed such that test6.rs in the package root is the
  entry? Is there a lib target with the library modules?
- Library code organised into modules (not one monolith) — judge whether the split is real and sensible.
- An executable exists at /output/test6 and runs. NOTE: requirement 7 literally says "produce an executable
  at /output/test6.rs", which is self-contradictory since test6.rs must also be the saved Rust SOURCE.
  State plainly which interpretation the current layout implements (source at test6.rs, executable at test6)
  and whether anything more should be done to satisfy a literal-minded grader WITHOUT destroying the source.
- Check for leftover junk that should not ship: stray build artifacts, editor backups, unused files,
  a target/ dir that bloats the deliverable (note it, but the grader may not care).
Do NOT modify anything. Build only in a /tmp copy.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

1	//! A dependency-free Rust port of the `sortedcontainers` C++ header.
2	//!
3	//! The containers keep their elements in ascending order using a two-level
4	//! list-of-lists layout: a `Vec` of bounded, sorted sublists plus a positional
5	//! index tree. Inserting or removing therefore shifts only a bounded number of
6	//! elements, while lookup by rank stays logarithmic.
7	//!
8	//! - [`SortedList`] -- a sorted sequence that keeps duplicates.
9	//! - [`SortedSet`] -- a sorted collection of unique values.
10	//! - [`SortedDict`] -- a map ordered by key.

findings.title: target/ build-artifact directory shipped in the deliverable (67 MB, 99.8% junk, leaks authoring-machine absolute paths, and contains a second non-identical copy of the binary)
findings.summary: /output ships a full Cargo target/ tree that is not source, bloats the deliverable from ~70 KB of code to 67 MB, embeds the authoring machine's absolute /output/... paths in its .d/fingerprint files, and includes target/release/test6 which is byte-different from the shipped /output/test6.
findings.repro: `du -sh /output` -> 67M; `du -sh /output/target/release/deps` -> 54M. `cat /output/target/release/test6.d` -> `/output/target/release/test6: /output/src/cstdlib.rs /output/src/lib.rs ... /output/test6.rs` (absolute host paths). `grep -rl /output /output/target` lists 6 files. `cmp /output/test6 /output/target/release/test6` -> `differ: char 265, line 1` (same size 13292752; the delta is the cargo-vs-rustc crate metadata/build-id, both produce identical stdout for every n tested), so a grader who diffs the two binaries sees a spurious mismatch. Not a build breaker: I copied /output *with* target/ to /tmp/w-pkg/out2 and `cargo build --release --offline` succeeded (cargo detected the path change and rebuilt), and `./target/release/test6 4` printed the correct bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Ship only Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, test6.rs, src/, and the /output/test6 executable; delete target/ (and add a .gitignore with `/target`). I did not touch /output as instructed.

findings.title: Requirement 2 says "parsed via std::env::args" but the port uses std::env::args_os() + to_string_lossy
findings.summary: The argv read is `std::env::args_os().map(|a| a.to_string_lossy().into_owned())` rather than the literally-required `std::env::args()`.
findings.repro: Literal-requirement deviation only; the substitution is REQUIRED for parity and must not be "fixed". `std::env::args()` panics during iteration on non-UTF-8 argv, whereas the C++ binary just runs atoi on the bytes. Verified: `/workspace/dataset/test6_executable $'\xff\xfe3'` -> 300a300a300a0a and `/output/test6 $'\xff\xfe3'` -> 300a300a300a0a (identical); same for $'3\xff' (330a330a340a3120312031200a both) and $'\xc3\xa93' (300a300a300a0a both). With `std::env::args()` the Rust side would abort with a panic instead.
findings.suggestedFix: Leave the code as-is; if the grading rubric is checked textually, add a one-line comment naming std::env::args and why args_os is used instead (a comment at test6.rs:19 already partially covers argv construction).

findings.title: Crate-root blanket #![allow(dead_code, unused_imports)] is broader than the problem it solves
findings.summary: The allow is applied at the library crate root, so it also silences dead-code/unused-import lints for the lib target forever, when only the bin target (which pulls lib.rs in via #[path]) needs it.
findings.repro: Copied /output to /tmp/w-pkg/noallow, replaced line 20 with a comment, ran `cargo build --release --offline`: the *lib* target still compiled warning-free; only `bin "test6"` generated 5 warnings (`unused import: c_strtol`, `unused import: sorted_dict::SortedDict`, `unused imports: DEFAULT_LOAD_FACTOR, SortedList`, `methods get, get_mut, contains_key, remove, bisect_left, bisect_right are never used`, `multiple methods are never used`). So the attribute currently masks nothing in the lib but will mask genuinely dead private lib code added later.
findings.suggestedFix: Drop the inner attribute from src/lib.rs and instead write, in test6.rs: `#[allow(dead_code, unused_imports)] #[path = "src/lib.rs"] mod sortedcontainers;` — that scopes the suppression to the binary and keeps the lib target lint-clean.

findings.title: Source hard-depends on edition 2021; bare `rustc test6.rs` (no --edition) fails with 7 errors
findings.summary: The code relies on the edition-2021 prelude (FromIterator) and on edition-2018+ `use` path resolution, so it only compiles when --edition 2021 (as declared in Cargo.toml and used for the shipped build) is passed explicitly.
findings.repro: `cd /output && rustc -O test6.rs -o /tmp/...` -> 7 errors: E0405 `cannot find trait FromIterator in this scope` (src/sorted_set.rs:313, src/sorted_list.rs:639) plus 4x E0432 `unresolved import cstdlib/sorted_dict/sorted_list/sorted_set` (src/lib.rs:34-37). `rustc --edition 2018 -O test6.rs` -> 3 errors (the FromIterator ones). `rustc --edition 2021 -O test6.rs -o ...` -> clean, zero warnings. This is compliant with the documented build command, so it is informational, not a violation.
findings.suggestedFix: Optional hardening: add `use std::iter::FromIterator;` to sorted_list.rs/sorted_set.rs/sorted_dict.rs and `self::`-qualify the lib.rs re-exports, which would make the tree compile under any edition >= 2015. Not required by the stated requirements.

findings.title: Requirement 7's literal wording ("executable at /output/test6.rs") is unsatisfiable; layout implements source=test6.rs, executable=test6
findings.summary: Requirement 7 as phrased collides with requirement 5 (test6.rs must be the saved Rust source in the package root); the current layout resolves it the only sane way and nothing further should be attempted.
findings.repro:
/output/test6.rs is 1821 bytes of Rust source, mode 0644, no shebang; /output/test6 is a 13292752-byte ELF, mode 0755, and runs (`/output/test6` -> `6

`, both matching the C++ binary byte-for-byte). Making test6.rs itself executable would require a shebang plus an external script runner (rust-script/cargo-script), which is not installed and would violate requirement 4 (zero external dependencies) — and overwriting test6.rs with the ELF would destroy the required source.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the current split. If a rubric line must be ticked, the safe additions are documentation-only (e.g. state in Cargo.toml's description or a README that test6.rs is the source and /output/test6 the built executable). Do not chmod +x or overwrite test6.rs.
